'This costs {r} less to play for each Runechant you control. Search your deck for a Runeblade aura with cost X OR LESS, put it into the arena, then shuffle. If X IS 2 OR MORE, this gets go again.'

Re-authored. Two defects. (1) The go again was gated on CHAIN_HIT_COUNT_GTE 2 -- the number of attacks that have HIT this combat chain, which has nothing to do with X and is normally 0 on a non-attack action played outside combat, so the clause never fired while the printed GoAgain paid out anyway. (2) It carried a PAY_LIFE 1 additional cost that appears NOWHERE in the printed text -- an invented cost, which is worse than a missing one because it silently makes the card unplayable at 1 life.

X is the card's variable cost (specialCost 'XX'), which play.py stamps as card.x_paid when the card is played; the {"type":"X"} amount reads it back. The same X bounds the search and gates the go again, which is why both read the one expression rather than a literal.

NOT MODELLED: 'costs {r} less for each Runechant you control'. cost_modifiers takes a condition and a flat delta, so it can say 'costs 1 less if you control a Runechant' but not a per-Runechant scale, and guessing a fixed number would be wrong in both directions. Flagged rather than approximated.
